questions.question: While travelling by bus, you see a passenger leave their mobile phone on the seat when they get off.
questions.questionHtml: While travelling by bus, you see a passenger leave their mobile phone on the seat when they get off.

options.text: Keep it with you for your own use

Try to chase the passenger and return it

options.text: Leave it there, thinking they will come back for it
options.html: Leave it there, thinking they will come back for it

questions.solution:
The most responsible and safe reaction is to hand it over to the conductor.

The conductor can officially record and store the item, making it more likely to reach the rightful owner.

Directly chasing the passenger may cause confusion or risk, while keeping it is unethical.

questions.question: Find the term which does not fit into the series given below: G4T, J10R, M20P, P43N, S90L
questions.questionHtml:
Find the term which does not fit into the series given below:

G4T, J10R, M20P, P43N, S90L
questions.solution:
1st letter:
G →(+3)→ J →(+3)→ M →(+3)→ P →(+3)→ S

3rd letter:
T →(−2)→ R →(−2)→ P →(−2)→ N →(−2)→ L

The number‐series 4, 10, 20, 43, 90 should follow the pattern ×2 + 1, ×2 + 2, ×2 + 3, ×2 + 4.
So, 10 is wrong and must be replaced by (4 × 2 + 1) i.e. 9.

Thus, the term J10R does not fit in the given series. The correct term is J9R.

questions.question: In a certain code, VISHWANATHAN is written as NAAWTHHSANIV. How is KARUNAKARANA written in that code?
questions.questionHtml: In a certain code, VISHWANATHAN is written as NAAWTHHSANIV. How is KARUNAKARANA written in that code?
questions.solution:
Divide the word into six sets of two letters each and label these sets from 1 to 6. Then, the code contains these sets in the order 4, 3, 5, 2, 6, 1 with the letters of sets 3, 2, 1 written in a reverse order. Thus, we have:

VI SH WA NA TH AN
1 2 3 4 5 6

→ NA AW TH HS AN IV
4 3 5 2 6 1

questions.question: If in a certain language, ‘oka peru’ means ‘fine cloth’; ‘meta lisa’ means ‘clear water’ and ‘dona lisa peru’ means ‘fine clear weather’, which word in that language means ‘weather’?
questions.questionHtml: If in a certain language, ‘oka peru’ means ‘fine cloth’; ‘meta lisa’ means ‘clear water’ and ‘dona lisa peru’ means ‘fine clear weather’, which word in that language means ‘weather’?
questions.solution:
In the first and third statements, the common code‐word is ‘peru’ and the common word is ‘fine’.
So, ‘peru’ means ‘fine’.

In the second and third statements, the common code‐word is ‘lisa’ and the common word is ‘clear’.
So, ‘lisa’ means ‘clear’.

Thus, in the third statement, ‘lisa’ means ‘clear’ and ‘peru’ means ‘fine’. So, ‘dona’ means ‘weather’.

questions.question: Which of the following diagrams best represents the relationship among these three classes? Males, Fathers, Doctors
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following diagrams best represents the relationship among these three classes?

Males, Fathers, Doctors
questions.solution:
All fathers are males, so the “Fathers” circle is completely inside “Males”.

Doctors can be male or female, so the “Doctors” circle partially overlaps “Males” (including Fathers) and also lies outside Males.

Some doctors can be fathers, some male doctors are not fathers, and some doctors are female.

questions.question: Statement: Should agriculture in rural India be mechanized? Arguments: I. Yes. It would lead to higher production. II. No. Many villagers would be left unemployed.
questions.questionHtml:
Statement: Should agriculture in rural India be mechanized?

Arguments:
I. Yes. It would lead to higher production.
II. No. Many villagers would be left unemployed.

options.text: Either I or II is strong
Both I and II are strong

questions.solution:
Both I and II are strong.

Argument I (Yes, higher production): Direct, relevant, and logical. Mechanisation typically increases efficiency, reduces losses, and raises output—exactly the policy goal. Hence strong.

Argument II (No, unemployment): Also directly relevant and socially significant. Large-scale mechanisation can reduce demand for manual farm labour in rural areas, risking job loss without parallel reskilling or alternative work. Hence strong.

questions.question: Statement “If you want to give any advertisement, give it in the newspaper X.” — A tells B. Assumptions: I. B wants to publicise his products. II. Newspaper X has a wide circulation.
questions.questionHtml:
Statement
“If you want to give any advertisement, give it in the newspaper X.” — A tells B.

Assumptions:
I. B wants to publicise his products.
II. Newspaper X has a wide circulation.

options.text: if only assumption I is implicit;
if only assumption II is implicit;
if either I or II is implicit;
options.html: if either I or II is implicit;

options.text: if both I and II are implicit.
options.html: if both I and II are implicit.

questions.solution:
“If” = conditional. It shows B may or may not want to advertise. So Assumption I (B wants to publicise) is not implicit.

The advice “give it in newspaper X” implies X is an effective medium for advertising. A paper is effective because it has wide circulation. Hence Assumption II is implicit.
